questions.question: The length of the base of a triangle is equal to the perimeter of a square whose diagonal is 7√2 cm and the corresponding height of the triangle is equal to the length of a side of the square whose area is 169 sq cm. The area (in sq cm) of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Base** of triangle = 4 × (Diagonal of square / √2) = 4 × 7 = 28 cm.

**Height** of triangle = √(Area of square) = √169 = 13 cm.

**Area** of triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 28 × 13 = 182 sq cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 182 sq cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diagonal of **Square₁** = 7√2 cm

Area of **Square₂** = 169 sq cm

**Formula Used:**

Side of square = Diagonal / √2

Perimeter of square = 4 × Side

Area of square = (Side)²

Area of triangle = (1/2) × base × height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b92d3824b34d14af6f3582d6d411437ff9107348f2b3c5c05b7b6b0832d7762.png] 

⇒ Side of **Square₁** = 7√2 / √2 = 7 cm

⇒ Perimeter of **Square₁** = 4 × 7 = 28 cm

⇒ **Base (b)** of triangle = 28 cm

⇒ Side of **Square₂** = √169 = 13 cm

⇒ **Height (h)** of triangle = 13 cm

⇒ **Area of triangle** = (1/2) × 28 × 13

⇒ Area = 14 × 13 = 182 sq cm

**∴ The correct answer is 182 sq cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Square Properties

Relationship between side (a) and diagonal (d): d = a√2. Area = a² = d²/2.

Area of Triangle (Heron's Formula)

For a triangle with sides a, b, and c: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c)/2.

Equilateral Triangle

Area of an equilateral triangle with side 'a' is (√3 / 4) × a² and height is (√3 / 2) × a.</p

questions.question: When white light is dispersed by a glass prism into seven colours, out of the following colours which colour will be deviated the least?

• The seven colours produced are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet, each having a different wavelength.
 
• The deviation of light depends on the wavelength; shorter wavelengths (violet, indigo) are deviated more than longer wavelengths (red).
 
• Among the given options, yellow light has a longer wavelength compared to indigo, blue, and green.
 
• As a result, yellow light will experience the least deviation out of the provided options when dispersed by a prism.

• Dispersion occurs because different colours of light travel at different speeds in a medium, leading to different angles of refraction.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index**
 
 
• The refractive index of a material varies with the wavelength of light, causing the separation of colours in a prism.
 
 
 
• **Application in Optics**
 
 
• Dispersion is utilized in various optical instruments and technologies, such as spectrometers and prisms used in science and industry.

questions.question: What are the basic building units of organisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Cells are the basic structural and functional units of all living organisms.
 
• They can exist as independent single-celled organisms or as part of a multicellular organism.
 
• Cells carry out essential processes such as metabolism, energy conversion, and reproduction.
 
• There are two main types of cells: prokaryotic cells, which do not have a defined nucleus, and eukaryotic cells, which have a defined nucleus and organelles.
 
• Cells are composed of various organelles that perform specific functions necessary for the cell's survival and proper functioning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tissues**

 
 
• Tissues are groups of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.
 
• There are four basic types of tissues in animals: epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues.
 
 
 
• **Organs**
 
 
• Organs are structures made up of different types of tissues that work together to perform specific functions within an organism.
 
• Examples include the heart, lungs, and brain in animals, and roots, stems, and leaves in plants.
 
 
 
• **Organ Systems**
 
 
• Organ systems are groups of organs that work together to perform complex functions necessary for the survival of the organism.
 
• Examples of organ systems in animals include the circulatory system, respiratory system, and digestive system.

questions.question: When an object falls under gravity, the object experiences:

options.text: a force only when it hits the surface of the earth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**an acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object falls under gravity, it experiences an acceleration due to the gravitational force exerted by the Earth.
 
• This acceleration is called gravitational acceleration and is denoted by 'g', which is approximately 9.8 m/s² near the Earth's surface.
 
• Gravitational acceleration acts on all objects equally, regardless of their masses.
 
• The direction of the acceleration is towards the center of the Earth.
 
• During free fall, the only force acting on the object is gravity, making it an ideal example of uniformly accelerated motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Force**

 
 
• Gravitational force is the attractive force between two masses.
 
• It is one of the four fundamental forces of nature.
 
• The strength of the gravitational force between two objects depends on their masses and the distance between them.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall**
 
 
• Free fall is the motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.
 
• In a vacuum, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass.
 
 
 
• **Terminal Velocity**
 
 
• Terminal velocity is the constant speed that a freely falling object eventually reaches when the resistance of the medium prevents further acceleration.
 
• At terminal velocity, the force of gravity is balanced by the drag force of the medium.

questions.question: When an iron nail is dipped into a copper sulphate solution, which substance gets displaced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an iron nail is dipped into a copper sulphate solution, a displacement reaction occurs.
 
• In this reaction, iron (Fe) displaces copper (Cu) from copper sulphate (CuSO₄) solution because iron is more reactive than copper.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.
 
• As a result, iron forms iron sulphate (FeSO₄) and copper is displaced from the solution.
 
• This type of reaction is an example of a single displacement reaction, where a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of their reactivity, from highest to lowest.
 
• Metals higher in the series can displace metals lower in the series from their compounds in solution.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reactions**
 
 
• These reactions involve a more reactive element displacing a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• Displacement reactions are commonly used in metal extraction and refining processes.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Displacement Reactions**
 
 
• Zinc displacing copper from copper sulphate solution: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.
 
• Magnesium displacing hydrogen from hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂.

questions.question: What is the path of an object when it is in uniform motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A straight line**__.

__
 
• In uniform motion, an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• The velocity of the object remains constant throughout the motion.
 
• The path of an object in uniform motion is a straight line because the direction does not change.
 
• Uniform motion implies that there is no acceleration involved in the movement of the object.
 
• This type of motion is an ideal concept often used in physics to simplify complex motion scenarios.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-uniform Motion**

 
 
• In non-uniform motion, the object travels unequal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• This type of motion involves changes in speed and/or direction, leading to acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Accelerated Motion**
 
 
• In accelerated motion, the velocity of the object changes over time.
 
• This can involve an increase or decrease in speed and can also include changes in direction.
 
 
 
• **Circular Motion**
 
 
• In circular motion, an object moves along the circumference of a circle.
 
• This type of motion involves a constant change in direction, leading to centripetal acceleration.

questions.question: An object is placed between the focus and the pole of a concave mirror, the image formed will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect and enlarged**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed between the focus (F) and the pole (P) of a concave mirror, the image formed is virtual.
 
• The image is erect, meaning it is upright and not inverted.
 
• The image is enlarged, appearing larger than the object.
 
• This type of image is formed behind the mirror.
 
• The rays appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror, leading to the virtual image formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Real Image**

 
 
• A real image is formed when light rays actually converge at a point.
 
• It is always inverted and can be projected onto a screen.
 
 
 
• **Concave Mirror**
 
 
• A concave mirror is a mirror with a surface that curves inward like a bowl.
 
 
• **Convex Mirror**
 
 
• A convex mirror has a surface that curves outward.
 
• It always forms virtual, erect, and diminished images regardless of the object's position.

questions.question: 3 pencils and 5 pens together cost ₹101, whereas 5 pencils and 3 pens together cost ₹91. The cost of 2 pencils and 2 pens together is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Add the two equations: (3 + 5) **Pencils** + (5 + 3) **Pens** = ₹101 + ₹91

8 **Pencils** + 8 **Pens** = ₹192

To find the cost of 2 **pencils** and 2 **pens**, divide the total by 4:

(8 Pencils + 8 Pens) ÷ 4 = ₹192 ÷ 4 = ₹48

**∴ The correct answer is ₹48.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 3 **pencils** and 5 **pens** = ₹101

Cost of 5 **pencils** and 3 **pens** = ₹91

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82a5854848680a999282254b92591b906108126995e7e16ec247b51d22b6d842.png] 

Let the cost of one **pencil** be x and one **pen** be y.

⇒ 3x + 5y = 101 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ 5x + 3y = 91 --- (Equation 2)

Adding both equations:

⇒ (3x + 5x) + (5y + 3y) = 101 + 91

⇒ 8x + 8y = 192

⇒ 8(x + y) = 192

⇒ x + y = 192 ÷ 8 = 24

Now, to find the cost of 2 **pencils** and 2 **pens**:

⇒ 2(x + y) = 2 × 24

⇒ 2x + 2y = 48

**∴ The correct answer is ₹48.**

**__Additional Information__**

Symmetric Linear Equations

Equations of the form ax + by = m and bx + ay = n are called symmetric equations. They are best solved by adding and subtracting them to find (x + y) and (x − y) values.

Unitary Cost Calculation

Total Cost ÷ Total Quantity gives the average cost per unit, which helps in finding costs for multiple units of a combined set.

Elimination Method

A general method where you multiply equations by constants to make the coefficients of one variable equal, then subtract to eliminate it.

questions.question: In a country, 55% of the population are females. 80% of the male population is literate. What percentage of females are literate if the total literacy rate is 58%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **Alligation Method**:

Ratio of **Male** to **Female** = 45 : 55 = 9 : 11

Let Female literacy be x%.

(80 − 58) ÷ (58 − x) = 11 ÷ 9

22 ÷ (58 − x) = 11 ÷ 9 ⇒ 2 × 9 = 58 − x

18 = 58 − x ⇒ x = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total Population** = 100 (Assumption)

**Females** = 55% of 100 = 55

**Males** = 100 − 55 = 45

**Total Literacy Rate** = 58% of 100 = 58

**Male Literacy Rate** = 80% of 45

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebdb3e2152ac0765ce9eeaef4f4313d8df194fc84ba205029dfc43c551d43063.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Literate people = 100 × (58 ÷ 100) = 58

⇒ Literate Males = 45 × (80 ÷ 100) = 36

⇒ Literate Females = Total Literates − Literate Males

⇒ Literate Females = 58 − 36 = 22

⇒ Female Literacy % = (Literate Females ÷ Total Females) × 100

⇒ Female Literacy % = (22 ÷ 55) × 100

⇒ Female Literacy % = (2 ÷ 5) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

Current **Sum of ages** = 51 + (3 persons × 8 years) = 75 years.

Total ratio parts = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 units.

15 units = 75 years → 1 unit = 5 years.

Present age of **eldest person** (6 units) = 6 × 5 = 30 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

Ratio of **present ages** = 4 : 5 : 6

Present Sum = Past Sum + (Number of Persons × Time Gap)

⇒ 15x = 51 + 24

⇒ 15x = 75

⇒ x = 75 ÷ 15 = 5

⇒ Present age of **eldest person** = 6x = 6 × 5 = 30 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

⇒ **Discount Amount** = MP − SP = 6 − 5 = ₹1.

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 6) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 16 2/3 %.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 2/3 %.**

__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the fundamental **Trigonometric Identity** cos² A = 1 − sin² A in the numerator.

Express the numerator as a product of factors: **(1 − sin A)(1 + sin A)**.

Cancel out the common term **(1 − sin A)** from both the numerator and denominator.

The resulting simplified expression for **y** is 1 + sin A.

**∴ The correct answer is sin A + 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** y = cos² A / (1 − sin A)

**Formula Used:** cos² A = 1 − sin² A and a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

⇒ y = (1 − sin² A) / (1 − sin A)

⇒ y = ((1 − sin A) × (1 + sin A)) / (1 − sin A)

⇒ y = 1 + sin A

**∴ The correct answer is sin A + 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Basic identities in trigonometry include sin² A + cos² A = 1, 1 + tan² A = sec² A, and 1 + cot² A = cosec² A.

Algebraic Simplification

The identity for the difference of two squares, a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b), is frequently used to simplify trigonometric fractions.

Domain of Expression

For a fraction to be defined, the denominator must not be zero. Here, 1 − sin A ≠ 0 implies sin A ≠ 1, which means A ≠ 90°.</p

questions.question: The smallest natural number that must be multiplied with 1083 to make it a perfect square is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Analyze the **prime factorization** of the given number:

1083 = 3 × 361 = 3¹ × 19²

For a number to be a **perfect square**, all prime factors must have even exponents.

Since 3 has an odd exponent (1), it must be multiplied by 3 to make its exponent even (2).

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 1083

**Formula Used:**

A natural number is a **perfect square** if and only if each of its prime factors can be grouped into equal pairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6717d7ee058a58f518335b41a46cf6e3d9aa1ae76d8cf06ed9e24265db08bb0d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Resolving the number 1083 into its prime factors:

⇒ 1083 ÷ 3 = 361

⇒ 361 = 19 × 19 = 19²

⇒ So, the prime factorization is: 1083 = 3¹ × 19²

⇒ Here, the prime factor 19 is paired, but the prime factor 3 is not paired.

⇒ To make it a perfect square, we must multiply the number by 3 to complete the pair of 3.

⇒ New number = 1083 × 3 = 3249 = (3 × 19)² = 57² (which is a perfect square)

⇒ Therefore, the smallest natural number to be multiplied is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Condition

A natural number is a perfect square if and only if all the exponents in its prime factorization are even. For example, N = p₁²a × p₂²b is always a perfect square.

Division to Make a Perfect Square

The smallest number by which a given number must be divided to make it a perfect square is the product of all its unpaired prime factors. This value is mathematically identical to the smallest multiplier required.

Square Root of a Large Number

The square root of a perfect square represented in prime factor form N = a²x × b²y is calculated as √N = ax × by.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To identify a **prime number**, check its divisibility by prime numbers up to its **square root** (√n).

For 373, **√373 ≈ 19.3**. Primes to check: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, and 19.

Checking 373: It is not divisible by any of these primes (e.g., 373 ÷ 17 = 21.94, 373 ÷ 19 = 19.63).

Since no prime factor exists up to 19.3, **373** is a **prime number**.

**∴ The correct answer is 373.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (1) 437, (2) 373, (3) 161, (4) 221.

**Formula Used:** A **Prime Number** is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35eadbbea9dc982fa905cf449756df98091fcb09423e96ac0e86ca224f7a8676.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For 161: 161 ÷ 7 = 23 (Divisible by 7, hence **Composite**)

⇒ For 221: 221 ÷ 13 = 17 (Divisible by 13, hence **Composite**)

⇒ For 437: 437 ÷ 19 = 23 (Divisible by 19, hence **Composite**)

⇒ For 373: √373 ≈ 19.3. Primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. None divide 373.

⇒ Therefore, 373 has no factors other than 1 and 373.

**∴ The correct answer is 373.**

**__Additional Information__**

Definition of Prime Number

A **prime number** is a positive integer greater than 1 that is divisible only by 1 and itself (e.g., 2, 3, 5, 7, 11...).

Composite Number

A **composite number** has at least one divisor other than 1 and itself. Every composite number can be factored into primes.

Checking for Primes (√n Method)

To determine if **n** is prime, test its divisibility by all primes **p** such that **p² ≤ n**. If no such **p** divides **n**, then **n** is prime.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are **co-prime** if their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is 1, regardless of whether the numbers themselves are prime.</p

questions.question: I walk at a speed of 10 km/h and reach the destination in 2 hrs, exactly on time. If I increase my speed by 5 km/h, how early would I reach my destination?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Speeds** (S₁ : S₂) = 10 : (10 + 5) = 10 : 15 = **2 : 3**

Since **Distance** is constant, Time ratio is the inverse: (T₁ : T₂) = **3 : 2**

Original Time (3 units) = 2 hours = **120 minutes**

Reduction in Time = 3 − 2 = 1 unit ⇒ 120 ÷ 3 = **40 minutes**

**∴ The correct answer is 40 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial speed = 10 km/h, Time = 2 hours, Speed increase = 5 km/h.

**Formula:** Distance = **Speed × Time** | Time = **Distance ÷ Speed**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f3ce0a63b51c7157343f5d5e59f4c1812e3e993bafe5e02471522d49f0e3d96.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = 10 km/h × 2 hours = **20 km**

⇒ New Speed = 10 + 5 = **15 km/h**

⇒ New Time taken = 20 ÷ 15 = 4/3 hours

⇒ Converting to minutes = (4/3) × 60 = **80 minutes**

⇒ Original Time = 2 × 60 = **120 minutes**

⇒ Time saved (Early reach) = 120 − 80 = **40 minutes**

**∴ The correct answer is 40 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed increases by a factor, time decreases by the same reciprocal factor.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **hours** to **minutes**, multiply by 60.

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by **(2xy) ÷ (x + y)**.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is obtained by subtracting x² - y² from y² - x²?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify terms: Let **A = x² − y²** and **B = y² − x²**.

Required calculation: **B − A**.

Calculation: (y² − x²) − (x² − y²) = y² − x² − x² + y² = 2y² − 2x².

Factorizing: 2y² − 2x² = **−2(x² − y²)**.

**∴ The correct answer is −2(x² − y²).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression to be subtracted: **(x² − y²)**

Expression from which to subtract: **(y² − x²)**

**Formula:**

Difference = **(Term 2) − (Term 1)**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Result = (y² − x²) − (x² − y²)

⇒ Result = y² − x² − x² + y²

⇒ Result = (y² + y²) + (−x² − x²)

⇒ Result = 2y² − 2x²

⇒ Taking −2 as a common factor: −2(x² − y²)

**∴ The correct answer is −2(x² − y²).**

**__Additional Information__**

Rules for Subtracting Polynomials

To subtract one algebraic expression from another, change the **sign** (from + to − or − to +) of every term in the expression being subtracted and then add the **like terms**.

Distributive Property of Signs

The negative sign outside a bracket affects all terms inside: **−(a − b) = −a + b** and **−(a + b) = −a − b**.

Like Terms

Addition and subtraction are only possible between **like terms**, which are terms that have the same variables raised to the same powers.</p

questions.question: If 48 : x :: x : 75, and x > 0, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When three numbers are in continued proportion **a : x :: x : b**, **x** is the **mean proportional**.

Direct formula: **x = √(a × b)**

x = √(48 × 75) = √(3600)

x = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Proportion 48 : x :: x : 75 and **x > 0**.

**Formula Used:** Product of Extremes = Product of Means

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/781141f95971365bbbfeb0eea72587e714cc4b26b1e5aa0af569a7845b1481fd.png] 

⇒ 48 : x = x : 75

⇒ 48 / x = x / 75

⇒ x × x = 48 × 75

⇒ x² = 3600

⇒ x = √3600

⇒ x = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is defined as **√(ab)**.

Third Proportional

If **a : b :: b : c**, then **c** is the third proportional to **a** and **b**, calculated as **c = b² / a**.

Fourth Proportional

If **a : b :: c : d**, then **d** is the fourth proportional, calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**.</p

__
 
• The statement "Heterotrophic organisms include plants" is incorrect. Plants are generally autotrophic organisms, meaning they produce their own food through photosynthesis.
 
• Heterotrophic organisms are those that cannot synthesize their own food and rely on other organisms for nutrition.
 
• Examples of heterotrophic organisms include animals, fungi, and many bacteria.
 
• Autotrophic organisms, such as plants, algae, and some bacteria, use light or chemical energy to synthesize food from inorganic substances.

• **Heterotrophic Nutrition**

• Includes various modes such as holozoic, saprophytic, and parasitic nutrition.
 
 
 
• **Mixotrophic Nutrition**
 
 
• Some organisms exhibit both autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
 
• Examples include certain protists and some plants like Venus flytrap.

questions.question: A and B can together complete a piece of work in 5 days. They worked together for 4 days and then B left. After another 2 days, A completed the remaining work. In how many days can A complete the entire work alone?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**A** and **B** finish the work in **5 days**, so in **4 days**, they complete 4/5 of the **total work**.

Remaining work = 1 − 4/5 = 1/5.

**A** completes this 1/5 work in **2 days**.

Total time for **A** alone = 2 × 5 = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by (**A** + **B**) = **5 days**, time worked together = **4 days**, time taken by **A** to finish remaining work = **2 days**.

**Formula:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **A** + **B**
 5
 5 units
 1 unit/day
 
 

 **A**
 10
 0.5 unit/day
 
 

⇒ Let **Total Work** = LCM(5) = **5 units**.

⇒ **Efficiency** of (**A** + **B**) = 5 ÷ 5 = **1 unit/day**.

⇒ Work completed by (**A** + **B**) in **4 days** = 4 × 1 = **4 units**.

⇒ Remaining work = 5 − 4 = **1 unit**.

⇒ **A** completes 1 unit in **2 days**.

⇒ **Efficiency** of **A** = 1 ÷ 2 = **0.5 units/day**.

⇒ Time taken by **A** alone = 5 ÷ 0.5 = **10 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Time and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time is x : y, then the ratio of efficiency is y : x.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed among workers in the ratio of their **efficiencies** or the actual **work done** by each person.

Combined Work Formula

If **A** can do a piece of work in x days and **B** in y days, then together they can do it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.</p

questions.question: If, in the quadrilateral JKLM, the measures of the angles J, K, L, and M are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 : 6, then the quadrilateral is a:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio** of angles J : K : L : M is 2 : 3 : 5 : 6.

Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 16 parts.

Since the total sum of angles is 360°, then 16 parts = 360° → 1 part = 22.5°.

Check **co-interior angle sums**: J + M = (2 + 6) × 22.5° = 180° and K + L = (3 + 5) × 22.5° = 180°.

When co-interior angles sum to 180°, the sides **JK and ML** are **parallel**.

A quadrilateral with only one pair of **parallel sides** is defined as a **Trapezium**.

**∴ The correct answer is Trapezium.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The measures of the angles J, K, L, and M of **quadrilateral JKLM** are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 : 6.

**Formula Used:** Sum of all interior angles of a **quadrilateral** = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0049cada488f17ba3d9019f52a75403de5f4fa63c5bc8a6bc3f14ee00eb1ec27.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the angles be 2x, 3x, 5x, and 6x.

⇒ 2x + 3x + 5x + 6x = 360°

⇒ 16x = 360°

⇒ x = 22.5°

⇒ Angle J = 2 × 22.5° = 45°

⇒ Angle K = 3 × 22.5° = 67.5°

⇒ Angle L = 5 × 22.5° = 112.5°

⇒ Angle M = 6 × 22.5° = 135°

⇒ Observe the sum of adjacent angles: J + M = 45° + 135° = 180°.

⇒ Similarly, K + L = 67.5° + 112.5° = 180°.

⇒ Since the sum of **co-interior angles** is 180°, the side **JK is parallel to ML**.

⇒ Because only one pair of opposite sides is parallel and the other sides (JM and KL) are not parallel (J + K ≠ 180°), the quadrilateral is a **Trapezium**.

**∴ The correct answer is Trapezium.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Trapezium

A **Trapezium** is a quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides. The angles on the same side of the non-parallel legs are **supplementary** (sum to 180°).

Sum of Angles in Polygons

For any polygon with n sides, the sum of internal angles is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n=4), the sum is 2 × 180° = 360°.

Parallel Line Properties

If a transversal intersects two lines such that the sum of **co-interior angles** is 180°, then the two lines are **parallel**.</p

questions.question: Using π = (22)/(7), find the total surface area of a closed cylinder having a base radius of 70 m and height of 110 m.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for **Total Surface Area** of a **closed cylinder**: 2πr(r + h)

Substitute values: TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 70 × (70 + 110)

⇒ TSA = 440 × 180

⇒ TSA = 79,200 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 79,200 m².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Base Radius** (r) = 70 m

**Height** (h) = 110 m

**Value of π** = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** = Curved Surface Area + 2 × Base Area

TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/995202e28eee811f01260913a21bfe5db6a5eb26dba9c40828433a0393a4def2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 70 × (110 + 70)

⇒ TSA = 2 × 22 × (70 ÷ 7) × 180

⇒ TSA = 44 × 10 × 180

⇒ TSA = 440 × 180

⇒ TSA = 79,200 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 79,200 m².**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The **lateral surface area** or **CSA** of a cylinder includes only the side walls and is given by 2πrh.

Volume of a Cylinder

The **space occupied** by a cylinder is its **volume**, calculated as Base Area × Height = πr²h.

Hollow Cylinder TSA

For a **hollow cylinder** with outer radius R and inner radius r, TSA = 2πRh + 2πrh + 2π(R² − r²).

Base Area

Since the base is a circle, the area of one **circular base** is πr².</p

questions.question: Two students appeared in an examination. One of them secured 9 marks more than the other and his marks were 56% of the sum of their marks. The marks obtained by them were:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **total marks** of both students be 100%.

One student secured **56%** of the total, so the other secured 100% − 56% = **44%**.

Difference in percentage = 56% − 44% = **12%**.

Given difference = **9 marks**. ∴ 12% ≡ 9 marks → 1% = 0.75 marks.

Marks are: 56 × 0.75 = **42** and 44 × 0.75 = **33**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 and 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference between marks = **9**. Higher marks = **56%** of the sum of marks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/37def73ff14247d6efbdafaba00faf71063c731c65a24d3d8a88ef5cb0c323b2.png] 

Let the marks obtained by the two students be **x** and **(x − 9)**.

According to the question:

⇒ x = 56% of [x + (x − 9)]

⇒ x = 0.56 × (2x − 9)

⇒ x = 1.12x − 5.04

⇒ 1.12x − x = 5.04

⇒ 0.12x = 5.04

⇒ x = 5.04 ÷ 0.12 = 504 ÷ 12

⇒ x = **42**

Marks of the second student = 42 − 9 = **33**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 and 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, convert 56% to a fraction: 56/100 = 14/25. This means if the sum is 25 units, the marks are 14 units.

Ratio Method

If Student A gets 56 units and the sum is 100, the ratio of marks A:B is 56:(100 − 56) = 56:44 = 14:11. Difference = 3 units = 9 marks, so 1 unit = 3 marks.

Linear Equations

Always define the variable based on the total sum or the larger value to keep the multiplication factors positive and manageable.</p
